messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired (PD#12345) — inference-queue backlog above critical threshold. queue_depth=14230, 95p_latency=2.2s, unacked_messages rising. Auto-remediation: none.

pagerduty: :bell: PD#12345 triggered — escalation policy: inference-oncall.

alex (oncall): acked. I'm taking this. Does anyone have quick eye on autoscaler metrics?

maria (sre): on it. pulling k8s and scaler metrics now.

chris (eng-runtime): seeing a pattern — autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts but nodes stuck in Provisioning state at cloud API. Could be quota or provider throttling.

alex (oncall): can you paste the autoscaler error?

chris (eng-runtime): sure — log snippet:

```
E0310 10:16:22.123 autoscaler.go:421] scaleUp error: failed to create nodegroup: CreateInstances API error: "QuotaExceeded: You have exceeded your CPU quota"
E0310 10:16:22.124 autoscaler.go:422] retrying in 30s
```

maria (sre): kubectl shows a large number of inference-worker pods Pending due to insufficient nodes: `kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending | wc -l` => 1523 pending.

sandeep (eng-infra): looking at cloud console — we've hit regional CPU quota for the fleet (region-us-west2). There are recent bursts from a test job that never cleaned up.

alex (oncall): ok — immediate mitigations? manual surge? fallbacks?

chris (eng-runtime): short-term: 1) increase autoscaler desired by temporarily overriding (if cloud quota allows) 2) evict non-critical workloads to free capacity 3) use warm pool or reserve pre-provisioned nodes. If quota is exceeded we need provider support or free up quota.

maria (sre): I'll start evicting batch/test jobs from the us-west2 cluster. Listing pods with label `team=test` and drain them.

ops-bot: running drain script: `scripts/drain-test-nodes.sh --region us-west2 --label team=test` — output: nodes found: 6, drained: 6.

sandeep (eng-infra): good call. Also submitted quota increase request to cloud console (support case #CC-78912). ETA unknown. Meanwhile we can reallocate reserved nodes from non-prod pools.

alex (oncall): can someone manually patch the horizontal autoscaler or scale the nodegroup to push a manual surge? I'll do a manual patch if infra gives thumbs up.

chris (eng-runtime): you can run: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed set-autoscaling ... --min-num-replicas=50` but we should avoid permanent change. Better: `gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize --size=50` for immediate surge.

sandeep (eng-infra): I'm ok to approve a temporary manual resize. Doing `resize` now to 48 nodes in inference-fleet-usw2.

alex (oncall): running k8s scale for static pods to accept work: `kubectl delete pod -l tier=warm-cache -n infra` to force warm cache restart across nodes.

maria (sre): monitoring queue. Prometheus shows queue_depth trending down from 14.2k -> 9.1k after evictions and node resize. Good sign but still high.

pagerduty: PD#12345 acknowledged by alex (oncall).

chris (eng-runtime): autoscaler logs after manual resize: `scaleUp: new nodes detected, starting node registration` then a bunch of `NodeReady` messages. However there's still a backlog because pod startup time + image pull ~30-45s.

alex (oncall): any sign of image-pull bottleneck? network egress?

maria (sre): some nodes reported high image-pull latency. We can mitigate by temporarily switching to smaller base image (if available) or using local registry cache. Ops-bot can prime cache.

ops-bot: priming local registry cache for inference-agent images — progress 40%.

sandeep (eng-infra): also seeing some older spot nodes getting preempted which reduced effective capacity earlier. I've adjusted instance policy to prefer on-demand for this surge.

alex (oncall): passing to chris for runtime tweaks, I'll keep monitoring and prep customer comms if needed. Handing off (10:23Z) to chris.

chris (eng-runtime): thanks. I'm toggling conservative-slo-mode to reduce per-request tokenization cost and prefer shorter compute paths: `./cli toggle-slo --mode conservative` — should drop CPU usage per request a bit.

maria (sre): queue_depth now 4.2k, 95p lat down to 1.0s. Still some tail errors: a few 5xx from worker initialization timeouts.

alex (oncall): do we know customer impact? any active customer-facing errors?

maria (sre): product logs show elevated errors for a couple high-traffic tenants, but most traffic is slower rather than errors. I started a Slack DM with support to flag top 3 customers.

chris (eng-runtime): adding a temporary routing rule to shed background /bulk endpoints to Dedicated pool to prioritize latency-critical routes. Patching now.

ops-bot: route update applied: /bulk -> dedicated-backup (rate-limited).

maria (sre): queue_depth 1.1k, 95p lat 0.7s, errors falling. Good trend.

pagerduty: PD#12345 resolved automatically (condition cleared).

alex (oncall): closing the PD but keeping thread open for postmortem notes. Immediate cause: regional CPU quota + spot preemptions causing autoscaler unable to provision in time; compounded by large test jobs occupying capacity.

sandeep (eng-infra): follow-ups: 1) finalize quota increase or rearchitect pool partitioning 2) implement guardrail to fail test jobs that request huge resources 3) add pre-warming scheduled during peak hours 4) improve autoscaler fallback to prefer on-demand when provisioning failures are detected.

chris (eng-runtime): runtime follow-ups: pre-pull images in warm pool, tune pod startup heavy paths, add a fast-path for small requests.

maria (sre): I'll file the incident (INC-2026-03) with timeline, metrics, and customer impact notes. Will assign action items to infra/runtime teams.

alex (oncall): thanks everyone. Handoff complete at 10:48Z — I'll update the incident ticket once Maria posts it. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: automated summary: PD#12345 — duration ~30m, peak queue 14.2k, mitigation: evicted test pods (6 nodes), manual resize + prefer on-demand (48 nodes), routing shed for /bulk, pre-warmed registry cache.

maria (sre): summary posted to INC-2026-03 and linked to this thread.

chris (eng-runtime): adding checklist item to ensure test jobs get a non-prod quota and can't hit prod pool.

alex (oncall): thread closed but keep eyes on related alerts for 2 hours. Good job. :rocket:
